why: The results are dominated by authorities (American Lung Association, ATS, FDA, county and hospital pages) that give safety framing only: "get a battery backup, car adapter or generator" with no product, runtime, price or cable detail. The FDA pages are about disasters generally, infant apnea monitors or device categories, not CPAP backup. The only source with anything checkable is a small runtime-estimator site (Wattcellar) working from specs, plus an affiliate planning guide; four results are empty PDFs. No major reviewer or authority tests or names CPAP backup batteries or power stations. ChatGPT will keep citing ALA/FDA for the safety lines, but a focused page naming specific batteries and power stations with per-night runtimes, DC cables per machine, current prices and tested codes would be the only product source in the set.
